format_version.description: The version of the format, 1 for this release.

market.description: Market data stored with the portfolio.

goals.description: Goals kept with the portfolio, each a plan with its name, in the order given.

description: A portfolio and, optionally, the market data to value it, in one versioned document.
title: Finalytics portfolio document

lot_method.description: How sales in this account choose lots, unless a sale says otherwise.

classifications.description:
Classifications by scheme, for grouping accounts: for example `owner: Alice` or
`wrapper: ISA`.

taxable.description:
Whether gains are taxed when they are realised: true by default. A retirement account,
or another tax-deferred or tax-exempt account, is not taxable, so rebalancing estimates
no tax on its sales.

Account.description: An account in a portfolio, such as a brokerage or custody account.

AccountId.description:
Identifies an account within a portfolio.

Identifiers are non-empty, have no leading or trailing whitespace, and are compared
exactly (case matters).

Currency.description: An ISO 4217 currency code, for example "USD".

Date.description: A calendar date in ISO 8601 form, for example "2026-11-02".

Decimal.description: An exact decimal number. Finalytics writes decimals as strings, such as "201.50", and reads strings or numbers.

quote.description: The currency it is priced in.

DocumentFxRates.description: The rates for one currency pair in a portfolio document.

pivot.description: The currency through which FX rates are crossed; USD by default.

max_carry_days.description: How many days a price or rate may be carried forward; 5 by default.

prices.description: Prices by instrument, in each instrument's currency.

fx.description: FX rates: units of `quote` per unit of `base`.

DocumentMarketData.description: Market data stored in a portfolio document.

oneOf.description: Every month (the default).
Every three months.
Every twelve months.

Frequency.description: How often a regular amount falls due.

name.description: The goal's name, such as "House deposit".

by.description: The month it is needed by.

oneOf.description:
An amount by a date, such as a house deposit, the money to start a business, or a
savings milestone. Met when the plan is worth at least `amount` at the start of the month
`by`.

name.description: The goal's name, such as "Retirement income".

every.description: How often it is paid: every month by default.

start.description: The month of the first payment.

end.description: The month of the last payment, or of the last month the payments run to.

oneOf.description:
An amount paid regularly from `start` to `end`, such as college fees or retirement
income. Met when every payment is made in full.

Goal.description: The goal a plan is tested against.

oneOf.description: A fixed rate a year, such as 0.025; 0 keeps every figure in money of the day.

A price index, such as the US consumer price index: one column of levels at least
monthly over the assets' history. Each simulated month takes the inflation of the same
past month as its returns.

Inflation.description: How prices rise, for amounts in today's money.

currency.description: The currency it is priced and traded in.

multiplier.description:
The value of one unit at a price of one: 1 for shares, the contract size for futures
and options.

classifications.description: Classifications by scheme, for example `asset_class: Equity`, `region: Europe`.

identifiers.description: Other identifiers by scheme, for example `isin` or `ticker`.

Instrument.description: Something a portfolio can hold, other than cash.

InstrumentId.description:
Identifies an instrument, for example `"AAPL"` or `"US0378331005"`.

Identifiers are non-empty, have no leading or trailing whitespace, and are compared
exactly (case matters).

oneOf.description: A share in a company.
A mutual fund, exchange-traded fund or similar pooled vehicle.
A bond, priced per unit (supply clean or dirty prices consistently).
A futures contract, priced per unit of the underlying with a contract multiplier.
An option, priced per unit of the underlying with a contract multiplier.
An FX forward, priced as its value per unit of notional.
Anything else.

InstrumentKind.description:
What kind of instrument something is.

Every kind is held and valued the same way, as a quantity times a price times a multiplier.
Derivatives and bonds are supplied already priced; Finalytics does not price them.

LotId.description:
Identifies a tax lot: the transaction that opened it, followed by `/` and the corporate
action that derived it, if any.

Identifiers are non-empty, have no leading or trailing whitespace, and are compared
exactly (case matters).

oneOf.description: First in, first out: the oldest lots first.
Last in, first out: the newest lots first.
The lots with the highest cost per unit first.
The lots with the lowest cost per unit first.
Every lot reduced in proportion, so each sale carries the average cost.
The lots named by the sale.

LotMethod.description: How sales choose which tax lots to close.

quantity.description: The number of units to take from it.

LotPick.description: A lot named by a sale or transfer, for specific identification.

name.description: A name for the mix, such as "Balanced 60/40".

weights.description: The weights by asset, adding up to one.

oneOf.description: The same weights throughout.

name.description: A name for the mix, such as "Glide path".

points.description: The weights by asset at each month, each set adding up to one.

oneOf.description:
Weights given at some months, moving in a straight line between them and held before the
first and after the last.

Mix.description:
What the money is invested in: fixed weights, or weights that change along a glide path.
The weights are restored every month.

block.description: The average length of a run, in months: 12 by default.

oneOf.description:
A stationary block bootstrap (Politis and Romano, 1994): runs of past months, all assets
together, of random length averaging `block` months, wrapping round at the end of the
history. The default, with blocks of 12 months.
A normal distribution with the assets' expected returns and covariance, per month.

Every stretch of the history as long as the plan, each once, in order: as many
simulations as there are stretches.

Model.description: How the simulations draw each month's returns.

Money.description:
An exact decimal amount in one currency.

Arithmetic between amounts checks that the currencies match and that no overflow occurs.
Amounts keep their full precision until they are rounded.

Month.description: A calendar month, written as "2030-06"; a date such as "2030-06-15" reads as its month.

name.description: A name for it in the report, such as "Monthly saving".

on.description: The month of a single payment.

every.description: How often a regular payment is made.

start.description: The first month of a regular payment: the plan's start by default.

end.description:
The last month of a regular payment: by default, the month before a target's date or
before the first goal payment, or the end of a plan without a goal.

growth.description:
How the amount grows a year in money of the day: with inflation by default, so that
it stays the same in today's money; 0 keeps it fixed in money of the day.

oneOf.description: Money paid in.

name.description: A name for it in the report, such as "Car".

on.description: The month of a single payment.

every.description: How often a regular payment is made.

start.description: The first month of a regular payment: the plan's start by default.

end.description:
The last month of a regular payment: by default, the plan's last month (the month
before a target's date, the last goal payment, or the end of a projection).

growth.description: How the amount grows a year in money of the day: with inflation by default.

oneOf.description:
Money taken out, as planned and not scored, such as a car bought along the way. When the
plan cannot cover it, what is left is paid.

PlanFlow.description:
Money paid into the plan, or taken out of it, other than the goal: once, in the month `on`,
or regularly, `every` month, quarter or year from `start` to `end`.

goal.description: The goal; without one, the plan is a projection to `end`.

chance.description: The chance of meeting the goal wanted, such as 0.8.

spare.description:
The chance from which the plan has room to spare: 10 points above `chance` by default,
at most 0.99.

start.description: The first month: the month after the assets' last date by default.

end.description: The last month of a projection without a goal.

start_value.description: What the money set aside is worth at the start, in today's money.

flows.description: Money paid in and taken out, other than the goal.

weights.description: What the money is invested in.

alternatives.description: Other mixes to compare on the same simulations, each named.

fee.description: The fee a year, as a share of the value, taken monthly.

inflation.description: How prices rise: required, as a rate or an index.

model.description: How each month's returns are drawn: a block bootstrap of 12 months by default.

expected_returns.description:
Expected returns a year by asset, in place of the history's: they shift the bootstrap's
returns and set the normal model's means.

simulations.description: The number of simulations: 10,000 by default.

seed.description: The seed of the random numbers: the same seed gives the same plan on every platform.

currency.description: The currency of the amounts, for the report.

name.description: The report's title: the goal's name by default.

PlanOptions.description: What a plan simulates and how.

base_currency.description: The currency results are reported in.

instruments.description: The instruments the transactions refer to.

transactions.description:
The transactions, in any order; they are applied by trade date, and in the order given
within a date.

PortfolioData.description:
A portfolio's records: its base currency, accounts, instruments and transactions. With market
data, they are everything Finalytics needs to keep the portfolio's books.

columns.description: The prices of each asset, one per date; absent where there is no price.

PriceTable.description:
The prices of several assets on the same dates, one column per asset. A missing price is
written as absent (`null`).

TimeSeries.description:
Values indexed by strictly increasing dates.

Construction checks the ordering, so every `TimeSeries` can be searched by date. A series is
serialised as `{"dates": [...], "values": [...]}`, and deserialising checks it again.

id.description: The caller's identifier, unique within the portfolio.

account.description: The account the transaction belongs to.

trade_date.description: The date the transaction takes effect for positions and performance.

settle_date.description: The date cash settles, if different from the trade date.

oneOf.description: Buy `quantity` units at `price` per unit, paying `fees` on top.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

price.description: The price per unit, zero or more.

fees.description: Commissions and other costs of the trade, added to the cost basis.

oneOf.description: Sell `quantity` units at `price` per unit, with `fees` deducted from the proceeds.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

price.description: The price per unit, zero or more.

fees.description: Commissions and other costs, deducted from the proceeds.

lot_method.description: Overrides the account's lot method for this sale.

lots.description: The lots to close, for specific identification.

oneOf.description: Cash paid into the account from outside the portfolio.
Cash taken out of the portfolio.
Units received from outside the portfolio.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

cost_basis.description:
The total cost basis carried over, in the instrument's currency. When absent, the
market value on the trade date is used.

acquired.description: The original acquisition date, when the holding period carries over.

oneOf.description: Units sent out of the portfolio. No gain is realised.

quantity.description: The number of units, greater than zero.

lot_method.description: Overrides the account's lot method for this transfer.

lots.description: The lots to send, for specific identification.

oneOf.description: A dividend received in cash.

withholding_tax.description: Tax withheld at source, in the same currency.

oneOf.description: Interest received in cash, from an instrument or on the cash balance.

instrument.description: The instrument that paid it, if any.

withholding_tax.description: Tax withheld at source, in the same currency.

oneOf.description: A fee not tied to a trade, such as a custody or management fee.
A tax not tied to a trade.
Cash converted from one currency to another.

A share split: every `from` units become `to` units, with cost basis unchanged. A reverse
split has `to` below `from`.

A spin-off: holders receive `ratio` units of a new instrument per unit held, and a share
`cost_allocation` (between 0 and 1) of the cost basis moves to the new units.

cost_allocation.description: The share of cost basis moved to the new units.

oneOf.description:
A merger or acquisition: each unit held becomes `ratio` units of `new_instrument`, plus
`cash_per_unit` in cash, which reduces the cost basis (gains beyond the basis are
realised).

ratio.description: New units per unit held; zero for an all-cash takeover.

cash_per_unit.description: Cash per unit held, in the held instrument's currency.

oneOf.description: The instrument's identifier changes; lots carry over unchanged.

A return of capital paid in cash, which reduces the cost basis (amounts beyond the basis
are realised as gains).

amount.description: The total amount, in the instrument's currency.

Transaction.description:
One event in the life of a portfolio.

Transactions are applied in trade-date order; transactions on the same date are applied in the
order given. Positions are booked on the trade date; the settlement date is recorded for cash
reporting.

TransactionId.description:
Identifies a transaction. Lots opened by a transaction take their identity from it.

Identifiers are non-empty, have no leading or trailing whitespace, and are compared
exactly (case matters).
